about: A13 language-lint vocabulary (ROADMAP M1.20, A13; DESIGN R-5.6.1), exported for the bank G6 lint (M3.2, A17). Generated by `npm run dump:language-terms` in the public repo; do not edit.

match.note: Each pattern is an ECMAScript regex source, matched case-insensitively between letters: anything but a letter delimits. Every example must match; no not_banned word may.

banned_terms.why: R-5.6.1 names it. §5.6: a short web test cannot flag autism (PPV about 9% at population base rates), so no copy may imply it can.
A former autism diagnosis label (R-5.6.1 "other clinical terms").
Acronym of the autism spectrum diagnosis (R-5.6.1).
Everyday euphemism for an autism label (R-5.6.1). "spectrum" alone is fine.
R-5.6.1 names it; the speed and memory axes (RT, PS, WM) must not read as an attention screen. The older acronym ADD is not listed: it collides with the verb "add".
R-5.6.1 names it. §5.6: it confounds emotion-reading scores, and that axis stays a skill measure (R-5.6.2).
Learning-disorder label; the reading-speed axis (M1.12, A10) must not read as a reading screen.
Learning-disorder label; the quantitative axis must not read as a maths screen.
Motor and writing disorder labels; RT, Corsi and coding must not read as motor screens.
Labels a person by neurotype (R-5.6.1). The blob describes skills, not who someone is; §5.6 (double empathy): a "neurotypical" key partly measures mismatch.
Clinical and educational classification categories (R-5.6.1). "disabled" alone is not listed (see NOT_BANNED).

§13: the app is not a clinical assessment; R-5.6.3: it never asks about diagnoses. Copy says what the scores are, not which diagnosis they are not (the one exception is the R-5.6.2 tooltip, an allowed text: see the header).
Medical outcome framing (§13: not a basis for decisions about health).
The DSM/ICD category noun (R-5.6.1).
§5.6: the deficit account is contested and a low score partly measures mismatch; R-5.6.4: lows are never framed as weaknesses. Also the D of ADHD.
Clinical deficit framing. The §13 skip-axis reasons should say "low vision" or "colour vision", not "visual impairment".
Medical framing of individual differences (R-5.6.1).
R-5.6.3: no questions about symptoms are asked or stored, and copy must not invite them.
Medical category noun (R-5.6.1).
R-5.6.1 "other clinical terms". A13: allowed only inside the §13 disclaimer ("clinical"), the R-5.6.5 sentence ("clinician") and the R-5.6.2 tooltip ("clinical").
§13: "Not an IQ test". An IQ is a normed score from clinical batteries (§2.1), and M1 shows no norms (A12). Allowed only inside the §13 disclaimer. "IQR" is fine.
Implies a clinical screening instrument, which §5.6 shows a short web test cannot be. "screen" and "screen reader" are fine.
Treatment framing (§13: not a basis for decisions about health).
Clinical specialties and their test batteries (§2.1); HumanBench is not one (§13).
Clinical deviance framing of a score; say "unusual".
Obsolete clinical label and a slur.
Named psychiatric or neurological conditions (R-5.6.1 "other clinical terms").

not_banned.add: The verb; the old acronym ADD collides with it (ADHD is banned).
not_banned.disabled: An HTML attribute and accessibility vocabulary.
not_banned.spectrum: Ordinary word; only the phrase "on the spectrum" is a label.
not_banned.health: In the §13 disclaimer itself; R-5.6.3 bans asking about it, not the word.
not_banned.anxious: Emotion vocabulary the Emotion Reading axis needs (R-5.6.2).
not_banned.sad: Emotion vocabulary the Emotion Reading axis needs (R-5.6.2).
not_banned.depressed: Emotion vocabulary; also keys "depressed" in input handling.
not_banned.depression: Economic history (reading passages) and emotion vocabulary.
not_banned.weakness: R-5.6.4 is a share-card rule (M1.18), not a word ban.
